# Environmental surveillance, One Health, and infectious disease transmission

We study how pathogens move among people, animals, and the environment — and how environmental surveillance can help us detect, understand, and prevent infectious disease.

<div class="eyebrow">What we study</div>

## Linking environmental evidence to infectious disease transmission

Our work combines environmental microbiology, epidemiology, molecular methods, genomics, and quantitative modeling to understand pathogen circulation across human, animal, and environmental systems.
:::

::: {.card-grid}
::: {.card}
<div class="card-kicker">01</div>

### Environmental surveillance

We develop and apply environmental sampling approaches to detect pathogens in wastewater, air, water, and other complex matrices.
:::

::: {.card}
<div class="card-kicker">02</div>

### One Health transmission

We study how pathogens move among humans, animals, and shared environments, with a focus on zoonotic and emerging infections.
:::

::: {.card}
<div class="card-kicker">03</div>

### Infectious disease dynamics

We combine environmental measurements with epidemiologic and genomic data to understand transmission, exposure, and population-level risk.
:::

<div class="eyebrow">Featured research</div>

## From environmental detection to transmission insight

Environmental surveillance can reveal pathogen circulation that traditional clinical surveillance may miss. Our work asks not only whether pathogens can be detected in the environment, but what those measurements tell us about transmission, exposure, and public health action.

[Read about our research →](research.qmd)
